parsed.explanation: The combined regime criminalises same-sex conduct nationally (up to 20 years plus mandatory whipping, expressly reaching tourists) and bars gender-nonconforming presentation in every state for Muslim residents, enforced by religious departments. State targeting of trans people is documented: a 2020 ministerial 'full licence' for enforcement against transgender persons, mobilisation of 122 officers to hunt one trans woman, raids on venues including a 2025 sauna raid with 208 arrests — 31 of them foreign nationals — faces leaked, and 2019 killings of trans women with impunity plus male-ward sexual violence in custody. Recourse is thin: courts strike provisions on federalism grounds without relief, a magistrate refused remand yet release was delayed. Enforcement of private conduct is uncommon and tourists 'rarely targeted', which keeps this above the 0.15 tier, but documented state-directed trans targeting, venue raids reaching visitors, and violent, remedy-free custody sit clearly in the High Risk band. Non-Muslim visitors face the Penal Code and policing levers rather than Sharia exposure; minors' specific treatment is undocumented.

entry_documents.exposure: No explicit visa rule for transgender visitors; only stated policy is a 2001 remark that gay diplomats would be deported, current status unsourced. Marker changes domestically are routinely rejected, but visitor documents are home-issued.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry friction is an open question rather than a documented exposure; foreign nationals were nevertheless arrested in the 2025 raid, showing visa status does not shield.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2025 sauna raid: 208 arrests under 377B including 31 foreign nationals; faces and details leaked; release delayed despite remand refusal; prison terms four months to three years with male-ward sexual violence documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A magistrate rejected the remand extension; legal-aid bailors mobilised; embassies intervened.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for presence in a queer venue leads into national Penal Code prosecution and religious-department enforcement; judicial relief operated slowly and without discipline of officers.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Sharia codes in all thirteen states criminalise 'posing as a woman'; courts may order up to six months' rehabilitation (one year in one state) and commit women to approved homes; venue raids by police and religious departments.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Constitutional rulings struck down one state's cross-dressing provision and sixteen provisions in another — federalism grounds only, no decriminalisation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Subnational religious enforcement layers on top of national code liability; strikes narrow nothing the traveller actually risks.

care_services.exposure: Discriminatory denial of health care to trans people documented; conversion therapy openly promoted; blood-donation ban. Mostly resident-facing; visitor care continuity is undocumented.
care_services.interaction: Ungazetted fatwa ends surgery access; practical reach unresolved in the record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing is direct: minister granted 'full licence' for enforcement against transgender persons (2020); 122 religious officers hunted a trans woman; government 'rehabilitation' retreats; media bans and censorship; hate-speech code offers no protection in practice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: International condemnation of the 2020 order; no revocation documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Religious departments, police and ministers jointly frame trans people as targets — the state is the principal threat-framer.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented; no youth-specific health, medication or enforcement finding appears.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Three trans women killed in under two months (2019), police mistreatment documented, impunity; strip-search and sexual assault of a trans woman by religious officials; one woman arrested 20+ times; 16 arrested at a wedding.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence clustered in 2019 with no trans-specific rate against the background homicide rate; dated but recent relative to the record, with no later counter-evidence of reform.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime law; constitutional challenges deny relief without decriminalising; ongoing raids into 2025 show the exposure unremedied.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal aid and bail mobilisation after the 2025 raid; minister floated revisiting provisions; communications code nominally covers orientation-based hate speech.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are episodic and non-systemic; unknowns include visa practice for trans visitors and current status of the 2001 deportation remark.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A's exposure is administrative exclusion and humiliation without custody; here documented arrests of foreign nationals, delayed release, and Sharia rehabilitation orders go materially further, so the case sits below that anchor.

0.25-D features selective morality enforcement, blackmail and brief detention; this regime adds documented state-directed trans targeting (ministerial enforcement licence, hunted fugitive), killings with impunity and sexual assault in custody — somewhat worse than the 0.25 tier.

0.15-C has organised sweeps with custody violence and coerced statements; this regime shares raids and custody violence but its enforcement against private conduct and tourists is 'uncommon'/'rarely targeted' and remand courts sometimes refuse extensions — not quite the 0.15 tier.
0.55-B's worst outcome is refused entry and delay; here imprisonment, whipping and killings are on the table for the outed traveller — far above this anchor.
0.75-C offers functional appeals, release policies and respectful training; this jurisdiction has no working remedy, no protections, and documented official hostility — categorically different.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a national criminal code (20 years plus mandatory whipping, applying to any person including tourists) layered with universal subnational bans on gender-nonconforming presentation for Muslims, enforced by religious departments acting under explicit state authorisation to target transgender people. Raids on venues reach visitors directly — thirty-one foreign nationals were held in the 2025 raid — and police leak detainees' identities while courts provide only slow, partial relief. Documented killings of trans women with impunity, sexual assault by officials, and male-ward prison violence establish severe worst-case outcomes, and the state's own hand (2020 enforcement licence, rehabilitation retreats, censorship) places the worst feature between tiers 2 and 1. The mitigating facts — rare targeting of tourists in private, episodic enforcement, occasional judicial pushback, humanitarian bail efforts — pull the score up from the 0.15 tier but cannot offset the documented, unremedied, state-directed exposure. Minors' treatment is undocumented and adds no countervailing evidence. Result: High Risk, low in band, at 0.22.
